Then the shape is identical across the 19 services because it comes from the baseline and not from a local class

  Scenario: AC6 Every business rule BR1 to BR8 is held by a criterion or a guardrail test (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline modules and a service generated from the service template
    When the guardrail and contract tests of the baseline run
    Then the build fails when a floating version range or a service-chosen version appears (BR1)
    Then the baseline carries no threshold, band, limit, rate, date or reference value (BR2)
    Then no log record, span attribute, metric label or event carries personal data (BR3)
    Then one W3C trace context spans REST, Kafka and Temporal (BR4)
    Then authorisation stays object-level in the owning service and the helper fails closed (BR5)
    Then every error is one RFC 9457 problem detail with the trace identifier and every command carries an idempotency key (BR6)
    Then configuration is read from the environment and the secret store and no business default replaces a missing key (BR7)
    Then no service, schema, topic, queue, schedule or screen is created by this story (BR8)

  Scenario: AC7 A status change the model does not allow is refused with no effect (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a service built with the baseline error handling module and its own status model
    When a command asks for a status change the model does not allow
    Then the command is refused with one RFC 9457 problem detail carrying the trace identifier
    Then no state changes and no event is published for the refused command
    Then a status change the model allows passes unchanged
